sources.citation: Wikipedia (EN) 'Suku language'; Persée searches for Suku/Piper (hits: Yembi Bouka 1994 Africana Linguistica 11; Daeleman & Meeussen 1983 Africana Linguistica 9; Bastin 2006 Africana Linguistica 12 — comparative Bantu papers that merely cite Piper 1977); Vanacker & Bostoen 2020 Gisamba paper (cites Piper 1977:17 for Kisuku lexical forms only).
sources.note: Nothing on Suku stress or accent in any of these; Wikipedia has no phonology section.

sources.citation: Grambank v1, language suku1259 (coder Johanna Nickel), 195 values all coded from Piper (1977:109-211). https://grambank.clld.org/languages/suku1259
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress/accent feature exists in Grambank. Comments: 'The definite and indefinite forms of a noun are marked by tonal marking (Piper 1977:121)'; 'the tonal marking of definite and indefinite forms is lost in possessive constructions (Piper 1977: 141)'. Confirms Suku is tonal (second-hand from Piper), silent on stress.

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only full phonology of Suku (Glottolog 'grammar'; Grambank coded entirely from it, pp. 109-211 on nominal morphology with tonal definiteness marking). Its phonology chapter is where a statement on Ton/Akzent/Betonung would be; every later comparative paper cites it as the Suku reference.
